title: Null infinity, Bondi news and classical memory

items.title: A smooth vacuum Bondi expansion
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Formal smooth asymptotically flat vacuum Bondi data at a null end; no global vacuum existence, exact finite-radius waveform, empirical claim, or conclusion about nature is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian tangent-bundle conventions of the suppliers. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval, $r_0>0$, and $\mathcal E=I\times(r_0,\infty)\times S^2$, where $S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ has its unit round metric $q_{AB}$ and area form $d\Omega$. Let $D_A$ be the Levi-Civita covariant derivative of $q$, and raise angular indices with $q^{AB}$. A **Bondi-Sachs end** is a smooth Lorentzian metric on $\mathcal E$ written in coordinates $(u,r,x^A)$, $A,B=1,2$, as

$$g=-\left(e^{2\beta}\frac Vr-r^2\gamma_{AB}U^AU^B\right)du^2-2e^{2\beta}du\,dr-2r^2\gamma_{AB}U^Bdu\,dx^A+r^2\gamma_{AB}dx^A dx^B,$$

where $\beta,V,U^A,\gamma_{AB}$ are smooth, $\gamma_{AB}$ is positive definite, $\gamma^{AC}\gamma_{CB}=\delta^A_B$, and $\det(\gamma_{AB})=\det(q_{AB})$. Thus $u=\mathrm{constant}$ are outgoing null hypersurfaces, $r$ is the area radius, and $x^A$ are constant along their null generators. This Bondi gauge has $g_{rr}=g_{rA}=0$.

A **smooth Bondi expansion** is such an end with the differentiated uniform expansions

$$\gamma_{AB}=q_{AB}+\frac{C_{AB}(u,x)}r+\frac{P_{AB}(u,x)}{r^2}+O(r^{-3}),\qquad \beta=O(r^{-2}),\qquad U^A=\frac{U^A_{(2)}(u,x)}{r^2}+\frac{U^A_{(3)}(u,x)}{r^3}+O(r^{-4}),\qquad V=r-2m(u,x)+\frac{V_{(1)}(u,x)}r+O(r^{-2}).$$

Here $C_{AB}$, $P_{AB}$ and the displayed coefficients are smooth sphere fields on $I$; the determinant gauge imposes $q^{AB}C_{AB}=0$ and $q^{AB}P_{AB}=\tfrac12 C_{AB}C^{AB}$. For every compact $I'\subset I$, angular chart compact set, and derivative multi-index $\alpha$ of total order at most two, the partial derivatives of each $O(r^{-k})$ remainder obey $\partial_u^{\alpha_u}D^{\alpha_x}\partial_r^{\alpha_r}O(r^{-k})=O(r^{-k-\alpha_r})$ uniformly as $r\to\infty$. Define the **mass aspect** $m$ by the $r^{-1}$ coefficient in $V$, the **Bondi shear** by $C_{AB}=\lim_{r\to\infty}r(\gamma_{AB}-q_{AB})$, the **Bondi news** by $N_{AB}:=\partial_u C_{AB}$, and the **geometric Bondi mass** by $m_B(u):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}m(u,x)\,d\Omega$. The future null boundary used here is the formal $r\to\infty$ boundary $\mathcal I^+=I\times S^2$ with coordinates $(u,x^A)$; no conformal completion is included in this definition. A **vacuum Bondi expansion** means, in addition, that the Ricci tensor $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ defined by the curvature convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] vanishes to the asymptotic coefficient orders under discussion, with no cosmological term.

references.title: Thomas Mädler and Jeffrey Winicour, Bondi-Sachs Formalism, arXiv:1609.01731 (2016), full 31-page PDF: §2, Eqs. (3)-(5), and §3, Eqs. (33)-(45)
Andrew Strominger, Lectures on the Infrared Structure of Gravity and Gauge Theory, Princeton University Press (2018), full lecture notes arXiv:1703.05448: §5.1, Eqs. (5.1.1)-(5.1.5)

items.title: Bondi supertranslations and their action on the shear
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Defines the fixed-frame supertranslation action on formal smooth Bondi data; the full asymptotic symmetry group and its charge algebra are outside scope, and no distinguished ten-parameter subgroup of Minkowski translations and proper orthochronous Lorentz transformations is selected.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian boundary conventions inherited from [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. On its formal boundary $\mathcal I^+=I\times S^2$, let $\ell_{\mathcal I}=\partial_u$ be the null-generator direction and let $q_{AB}$ be the unit round metric on the cuts; the degenerate boundary metric is $q_{AB}dx^A dx^B$ with kernel $\mathbb R\ell_{\mathcal I}$. A **fixed Bondi frame** here means the chosen Bondi-Sachs chart and gauge $(u,r,x^A)$ of [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]], including $g_{rr}=g_{rA}=0$ and $\det\gamma=\det q$, with the round cut metric $q_{AB}$ held fixed. It is a chart/gauge choice, not an observer congruence or tetrad. An **infinitesimal supertranslation** is the asymptotic vector field parametrized by a smooth real function $f:S^2\to\mathbb R$ whose leading boundary action is $\delta_fu=f(x)$ and whose leading bulk generator is

$$\xi_f=f\,\partial_u-\frac1rD^Af\,\partial_A+\frac12D^AD_Af\,\partial_r+O(r^{-1})\partial_u+O(r^{-2})\partial_A+O(r^{-1})\partial_r.$$

The displayed leading terms preserve Bondi gauge and the fixed round cut metric to the asymptotic orders used here; the omitted terms are not part of this definition. We use the active convention $\delta_f=\mathcal L_{\xi_f}$. Its action on the shear and news of [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]] is

$$\delta_f C_{AB}=fN_{AB}-2D_AD_Bf+q_{AB}D^CD_Cf,\qquad \delta_f N_{AB}=f\,\partial_uN_{AB}.$$

The **finite active boundary supertranslation** with parameter $f$ is the map $\Phi_f(u,x)=(u+f(x),x)$ on
$$\mathcal D_f:=\{(u,x)\in I\times S^2:u+f(x)\in I\}.$$
It is a diffeomorphism from $\mathcal D_f$ onto $\mathcal D_{-f}$, with inverse $\Phi_{-f}$. If $I=\mathbb R$, it is a diffeomorphism of all of $\mathcal I^+$; for a shorter retarded-time interval the action is defined on this overlap only. In the same active convention, its induced action on the boundary shear and news is

$$C^{(f)}_{AB}(u,x)=C_{AB}(u+f(x),x)-2D_AD_Bf(x)+q_{AB}D^CD_Cf(x),\qquad N^{(f)}_{AB}(u,x)=N_{AB}(u+f(x),x),\quad (u,x)\in\mathcal D_f.$$

Differentiating these formulas for the parameter $tf$ at $t=0$ recovers the infinitesimal formulas above. This definition gives only the boundary action and induced shear/news; it does not specify the full finite bulk coordinate transformation.

The function $f$ carries length units when the retarded coordinate $u$ is read in SI geometric coordinates; the sphere derivatives and angular coordinates are dimensionless. The Hessian term is trace-free because $q^{AB}q_{AB}=2$. When $N_{AB}=0$, an infinitesimal supertranslation therefore changes a time-independent shear by the sphere trace-free Hessian while leaving the news zero.

references.title: Andrew Strominger, Lectures on the Infrared Structure of Gravity and Gauge Theory, Princeton University Press (2018), full lecture notes arXiv:1703.05448: §5.2.1, Eqs. (5.2.1)-(5.2.6), and §5.2.1 discussion of the absence of a preferred Poincare subgroup
Thomas Mädler and Jeffrey Winicour, Bondi-Sachs Formalism, arXiv:1609.01731 (2016), full 31-page PDF: §4, Eqs. (78)-(80), BMS generators and the finite supertranslation of retarded time and shear

items.title: Bondi mass-aspect constraint coefficient
items.design_state: Draft authored; local coefficient expansion escalated for owner resolution.
items.physical_scope: Conditional coefficient identity for a smooth Ricci-flat Bondi expansion; no global vacuum solution, radiation measurement, or physical validity claim is asserted.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian bundle conventions of the suppliers. Let a vacuum Bondi expansion be as in [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]], with $R_{ab}=0$ in the curvature convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Then, for the mass aspect $m$, shear $C_{AB}$, news $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}$, unit sphere metric $q_{AB}$ and its Levi-Civita derivative $D_A$ specified there,

$$\partial_um=\frac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\frac18N_{AB}N^{AB}.$$

The identity is the leading supplementary vacuum Einstein coefficient at future null infinity; it is not an exact finite-radius equation.

references.title: Thomas Mädler and Jeffrey Winicour, Bondi-Sachs Formalism, arXiv:1609.01731 (2016), full 31-page PDF: §3, Eqs. (28)-(58), especially the news convention (42), determinant identity (36), radial hierarchy (46)-(57), and mass-aspect equation (58)
Andrew Strominger, Lectures on the Infrared Structure of Gravity and Gauge Theory, Princeton University Press (2018), full lecture notes arXiv:1703.05448: §5.2.1, Eqs. (5.2.8)-(5.2.9)

items.strategy:
**Given:** [F1]–[F3] and [A1]–[A2] of the current lemma. Write $E=e^{2\beta}$, $h_{AB}=r^2\gamma_{AB}$, $w^A=U^A_{(2)}$, $w_A=q_{AB}w^B$, $Q_A=\partial_A\log\sqrt{\det q}$, and a dot for $\partial_u$. All estimates below are uniform on the compact retarded-time and angular-chart sets specified in [F1].

1.1 Metric compatibility and zero torsion give $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{cd}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc})$: lower the output index in metric compatibility and add the two cyclic equations minus the third. Multiplication of the Bondi metric by $g^{ur}=-E^{-1}$, $g^{rr}=E^{-1}V/r$, $g^{rA}=-E^{-1}U^A$, $g^{AB}=h^{AB}$ and $g^{uu}=g^{uA}=0$ gives the identity matrix. Its determinant is $-E^2r^4\det q$. Differentiating a determinant gives $\Gamma^a{}_{ab}=\partial_b\log\sqrt{|\det g|}$, so the traces are exactly $T_u:=\Gamma^a{}_{au}=2\dot\beta$, $T_r:=\Gamma^a{}_{ar}=2/r+2\beta_r$ and $T_A:=\Gamma^a{}_{aA}=Q_A+2\beta_A$. In particular $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma^{-1}\dot\gamma)=0$ exactly; no trace-free part of $P_{AB}$ has been removed. Contracting [F3] using [F2] gives $\operatorname{Ric}_{bc}=\partial_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}-\partial_cT_b+\Gamma^a{}_{bc}T_a-\Gamma^a{}_{cd}\Gamma^d{}_{ba}$. [F1, F2, F3, A1, algebra]

2.1 The given differentiated expansions imply $E=1+O(r^{-2})$, $h_{AB}=r^2q_{AB}+rC_{AB}+O(1)$, $h^{AB}=r^{-2}q^{AB}-r^{-3}C^{AB}+O(r^{-4})$, $g_{uu}=-1+2m/r+O(r^{-2})$ and $g_{uA}=-w_A+O(r^{-1})$. These follow directly from $g_{uu}=-EV/r+h_{AB}U^AU^B$ and $g_{uA}=-h_{AB}U^B$. A radial derivative lowers each remainder's order by one, and time or angular derivatives through total order two preserve its order. Products and inverses have these same differentiated bounds, since their denominators tend uniformly to nonzero ones. Every differentiated expression below uses at most two derivatives of the metric coefficients. Thus these are the existing differentiated hypotheses, not a termwise differentiability assumption beyond them. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For the radial constraint put $H^B{}_A:=\Gamma^B{}_{rA}$ and $T^r{}_A:=\Gamma^r{}_{rA}$. The Christoffel formula of step 1.1 gives the exact identities $\Gamma^u{}_{rA}=0$, $\Gamma^u{}_{rr}=\Gamma^B{}_{rr}=0$, $\Gamma^r{}_{rr}=2\beta_r$, $H^B{}_A=\tfrac12h^{BC}\partial_rh_{AC}$, and $T^r{}_A=\beta_A+(2E)^{-1}h_{AB}\partial_rU^B$. Hence $H^B{}_A=\delta^B_A/r-C^B{}_A/(2r^2)+O(r^{-3})$ and $T^r{}_A=-w_A/r+O(r^{-2})$. Also $\Gamma^u{}_{AB}=(2E)^{-1}\partial_rh_{AB}=O(r)$ and $\Gamma^B{}_{ru}=\tfrac12h^{BC}(\partial_rg_{uC}+\partial_CE)=O(r^{-4})$. The angular symbols are exactly $\Gamma^C{}_{AB}=\Gamma[\gamma]^C{}_{AB}+(2E)^{-1}U^C\partial_rh_{AB}$. Their difference from the round connection is $S^C{}_{AB}:=\Gamma^C{}_{AB}-\Gamma[q]^C{}_{AB}=\{D_AC^C{}_B+D_BC^C{}_A-D^CC_{AB}\}/(2r)+w^Cq_{AB}/r+O(r^{-2})$, obtained by inserting $\gamma=q+C/r+O(r^{-2})$ in its connection formula. Since $q^{AB}C_{AB}=0$, its contracted leading coefficient is $S^C{}_{AC}=w_A/r+O(r^{-2})$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 For the supplementary coefficient, set $K^a{}_b:=\Gamma^a{}_{ub}$. Using the exact traces from step 1.1 and combining $\partial_AK^A{}_u+Q_AK^A{}_u=D_AK^A{}_u$, the Ricci formula is exactly $\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}=\partial_uK^u{}_u+\partial_rK^r{}_u+D_AK^A{}_u-2\ddot\beta+2\dot\beta K^u{}_u+(2/r+2\beta_r)K^r{}_u+2\beta_AK^A{}_u-K^a{}_bK^b{}_a$. The Christoffel formula gives $K^u{}_u=2\dot\beta+(2E)^{-1}\partial_rg_{uu}$ exactly. It also gives $K^r{}_u=-\dot m/r+O(r^{-2})$ and $K^A{}_u=-\dot w^A/r^2+O(r^{-3})$: the leading terms come respectively from $\tfrac12g^{ru}\partial_ug_{uu}$ and $h^{AB}\partial_ug_{uB}$, while all other terms have the indicated lower orders. Therefore $\partial_uK^u{}_u-2\ddot\beta=-\dot m/r^2+O(r^{-3})$, $\partial_rK^r{}_u=\dot m/r^2+O(r^{-3})$, $D_AK^A{}_u=-D_A\dot w^A/r^2+O(r^{-3})$ and $(2/r)K^r{}_u=-2\dot m/r^2+O(r^{-3})$. The remaining three terms involving a derivative of $\beta$ times a $K$ are $O(r^{-4})$. The remainder differentiations here are covered by step 2.1. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Expand the contracted Ricci formula of step 1.1 for $(b,c)=(r,A)$. The angular derivative and background-connection terms combine into $D_BH^B{}_A$. The derivative $-\partial_AT_r=-2\partial_A\beta_r$ is $O(r^{-3})$. In the final quadratic sum, the only non-background terms possibly of order $r^{-2}$ are $S^C{}_{AB}H^B{}_C$ and $H^C{}_AT^r{}_C$: their coefficients are respectively $w_A$ and $-w_A$, by step 3.1, so they cancel. The other potentially large product $\Gamma^u{}_{AB}\Gamma^B{}_{ru}$ is $O(r^{-3})$; products with $\Gamma^u{}_{rA},\Gamma^u{}_{rr},\Gamma^B{}_{rr}$ vanish, and products involving $\beta_r$ or $\beta_A$ are $O(r^{-3})$ or smaller. Consequently $\operatorname{Ric}_{rA}=\partial_rT^r{}_A+D_BH^B{}_A+(2/r)T^r{}_A+O(r^{-3})=r^{-2}(-w_A-\tfrac12D_BC^B{}_A)+O(r^{-3})$. The first, second and third terms contribute respectively $w_A$, $-\tfrac12D_BC^B{}_A$ and $-2w_A$. Vacuum [A2] therefore gives $w^A=-\tfrac12D_BC^{AB}$ without determining $U^A_{(3)}$ or any trace-free coefficient of $P_{AB}$. [F1, F2, F3, A2, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 To exhibit every possible quadratic contribution, the same Christoffel formula gives $K^u{}_r=0$, $K^u{}_A=\beta_A+(2E)^{-1}\partial_rg_{uA}=O(r^{-2})$, $K^r{}_r=O(r^{-2})$, $K^r{}_A=O(r^{-1})$, $K^A{}_r=O(r^{-4})$, and $K^A{}_B=\tfrac12h^{AC}\partial_uh_{BC}+O(r^{-2})=N^A{}_B/(2r)+O(r^{-2})$; also $K^u{}_u=O(r^{-2})$, $K^r{}_u=O(r^{-1})$ and $K^A{}_u=O(r^{-2})$ by step 3.2. Thus in $K^a{}_bK^b{}_a$ the $uu$ and $rr$ diagonal products are $O(r^{-4})$, the $ur$ pair vanishes, the $uA$ pair is $O(r^{-4})$, the $rA$ pair is $O(r^{-5})$, and only the angular block contributes at order $r^{-2}$, giving $K^A{}_BK^B{}_A=N_{AB}N^{AB}/(4r^2)+O(r^{-3})$. This exhausts the contraction, rather than omitting uncomputed subleading terms. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 Combining steps 3.2 and 4.2 proves $\operatorname{Ric}_{uu}=r^{-2}(-2\dot m-D_A\dot w^A-\tfrac14N_{AB}N^{AB})+O(r^{-3})$. The determinant identity in step 1.1 cancelled the entire time derivative of the angular determinant before expansion; in particular its $r^{-2}$ trace combination $\operatorname{tr}_qP-\tfrac12C_{AB}C^{AB}$ and its first two time derivatives vanish. All remaining occurrences of $P_{AB}$ in the angular $K$ block have order $r^{-2}$ and hence enter its square only at $r^{-3}$ or below. Similarly $U^A_{(3)}$ affects $K^A{}_u$ only at $r^{-3}$ and $K^r{}_u$ only at $r^{-2}$, while $V_{(1)}$ affects the latter only at $r^{-2}$; radial differentiation or multiplication by $2/r$ then lowers these to $r^{-3}$. No coefficient called $\beta_{(3)}$ need exist: the whole $\beta$ time-derivative cancellation is exact, and the remaining derivative products have already been bounded. Since $q$ and $D$ do not depend on $u$, step 4.1 gives $D_A\dot w^A=-\tfrac12D_AD_BN^{AB}$. Vacuum [A2] now makes the displayed $r^{-2}$ coefficient zero and yields $\partial_um=\tfrac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\tfrac18N_{AB}N^{AB}$, with no additional choice use or asymptotic restriction. [A1, A2, step 1.1, step 4.1, step 3.2, step 4.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Classical shear memory and the leading displacement approximation
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Conditional classical Bondi-boundary identity, formal first-order Jacobi response, and controlled actual Jacobi displacement/velocity estimate for a fixed compact tube, interval and smooth normalized local metric family; no uncontrolled finite-amplitude, observed, or quantized-gravity claim.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and a smooth Bondi expansion as in [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. For $u_1<u_2$ in its retarded-length interval, define $\Delta C_{AB}:=C_{AB}(u_2)-C_{AB}(u_1)$. Then

$$\Delta C_{AB}=\int_{u_1}^{u_2}N_{AB}(u)\,du.$$

For the detector clause, fix an angular point $x\in S^2$ and a large fixed area radius $r>r_0$. In the local flat approximation choose the future unit observer $n=\partial_0$ and outward unit propagation direction $\hat k=\partial_3$ of [[def-gr-wave-screen-and-tt-projection]], so the positive screen is $\Sigma(n,\hat k)=\operatorname{span}(\partial_1,\partial_2)$. Let $\iota:S^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be the unit-sphere inclusion; $d\iota_x$ identifies $T_xS^2$ isometrically, for $q$, with the plane orthogonal to $\iota(x)$. Choose axes with $e_3=\iota(x)$ and a fixed ordered orthonormal screen basis $e_1,e_2$ corresponding to a $q$-orthonormal basis of $T_xS^2$. Use adapted inertial coordinates with $x^0=ct$ and $x^3$ in the $\hat k$ direction. The background central worldline is the restriction to $[u_1,u_2]$ of the smooth future-directed timelike affine geodesic $\gamma_0(u)=(x^0=u+r,x^1=0,x^2=0,x^3=r)$; its affine parameter $u$ is also proper-length parameter, and on it the Bondi retarded coordinate is $u=x^0-r$.

A **linear transverse detector approximation** here is the formal flat first-order model with a dimensionless screen-TT profile $H_{AB}(u)=C_{AB}(u,x)/r+\rho_{AB}(u,r,x)$ in the chosen basis, extended on an open tube $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^4$ around $\gamma_0([u_1,u_2])$ as the planar perturbation $h_{AB}(x^0,x^3)=H_{AB}(x^0-x^3)$ with all other components zero. Take $H$ as the first-order coefficient of a smooth flat linearized metric family on $\Omega$; only this coefficient is used. Assume the profile has a smooth extension outside $[u_1,u_2]$; only its values on this interval enter. For $j=0,1,2$, assume $\sup_{u\in[u_1,u_2]}|\partial_u^j\rho_{AB}(u,r,x)|\le K_jr^{-2}$, where the constants $K_j$ are uniform on the fixed interval and angular patch and have dimensions $\mathrm{length}^{2-j}$. Let $s_0^A$ be any initial screen-separation components in the fixed basis, with zero initial relative velocity. Its **formal first-order response** $\delta s^A$ is the unique solution of the linearized screen Jacobi equation

$$\partial_u^2\delta s^A=\frac12\partial_u^2H^A{}_B\,s_0^B,\qquad \delta s^A(u_1)=0,\qquad \partial_u\delta s^A(u_1)=0,$$

with angular indices raised using $q^{AB}$. Assume $N_{AB}(u_1)=N_{AB}(u_2)=0$. This formal clause is a first-order response coefficient only; its quantitative realization is stated separately below. Then

$$\delta s^A(u_2)=\frac{1}{2r}\Delta C^A{}_B\,s_0^B+O(r^{-2}|s_0|).$$

Under the same approximation, the endpoint relative screen velocity has first-order response $\partial_u\delta s^A(u_2)=O(r^{-2}|s_0|)$, so it has no leading $r^{-1}$ contribution when the news vanishes at both cuts.

The error constants depend on the fixed compact interval, angular patch and the $K_j$ bounds. No exact finite-radius identity $H_{AB}=C_{AB}/r$ is asserted.

A quantitative amplitude statement is also available. Fix $r$, the angular point, and the interval $[u_1,u_2]$, and let $\Omega$ contain a compact coordinate tube around $\gamma_0([u_1,u_2])$. Supply any smooth flat linearized family
$$g_{ab}(\lambda,x)=\eta_{ab}+\lambda h_{ab}(x)+\lambda^2k_{ab}(\lambda,x)$$
on this tube, in the exact sense of [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]], with the planar first-order coefficient $h_{AB}=H_{AB}(x^0-x^3)$ above and all other $h_{ab}=0$. The normalized remainder $k$ is smooth jointly in $(\lambda,x)$, and $\lambda$ is a dimensionless amplitude parameter. For small $|\lambda|$, use the future cone containing $\partial_0$ on a smaller tube. Issue the timelike geodesic $\gamma_\lambda$ from $\gamma_0(u_1)$ with unit initial velocity $\partial_0/\sqrt{-g_\lambda(\partial_0,\partial_0)}$. Choose a smooth initial orthonormal spatial frame tending to $(\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)$ at $\lambda=0$, and parallel-transport it along $\gamma_\lambda$. Let $J_\lambda$ be the exact Jacobi field with initial value $s_0^AE_{A,\lambda}(u_1)$ and covariant initial derivative zero, and define $s_\lambda^A(u):=g_\lambda(J_\lambda,E_{A,\lambda})$, $A=1,2$. These are screen components in the transported frame; initial rest is covariant rest, not a coordinate-velocity condition. The geodesics, frames and Jacobi fields exist on the full fixed interval for sufficiently small $|\lambda|$, and $J_\lambda$ is realizable as a smooth timelike geodesic variation. There are constants for this fixed tube, interval and normalized family such that
$$s_\lambda(u_2)-s_0=\frac{\lambda}{2r}\Delta C\,s_0+O(|\lambda|r^{-2}|s_0|)+O(\lambda^2|s_0|),\qquad s_\lambda'(u_2)=O(|\lambda|r^{-2}|s_0|)+O(\lambda^2|s_0|).$$
More precisely, the actual screen components equal $s_0+\lambda\delta s+O(\lambda^2|s_0|)$, and their derivatives equal $\lambda\delta s'+O(\lambda^2|s_0|)$, uniformly on the interval. The first-order $r^{-2}$ constants are uniform wherever the stated $K_j$ bounds are uniform; the amplitude-squared constants here are for fixed $r$ and the chosen family and tube. No uniformity of those constants as $r\to\infty$ is asserted without uniform family bounds. The parameter $\lambda$ is not identified with $\sup|H|$. This is a local metric-family estimate, not an error estimate comparing a full Bondi spacetime with its detector approximation.

references.title: Thomas Mädler and Jeffrey Winicour, Bondi-Sachs Formalism, arXiv:1609.01731 (2016), full 31-page PDF: §3, Eqs. (37), (40)-(43), and §4, supertranslation action on shear

Andrew Strominger, Lectures on the Infrared Structure of Gravity and Gauge Theory, Princeton University Press (2018), full lecture notes arXiv:1703.05448: §6, Eqs. (6.0.1)-(6.0.3), geodesic-deviation and displacement memory

items.title: Integrated vacuum Bondi mass loss
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A conditional consequence of the smooth Ricci-flat Bondi expansion; the mass monotonicity is a model deduction and not evidence that a physical system satisfies the hypotheses.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice for the smooth Lorentzian sphere-bundle convention of [[def-gr-fx-bondi-expansion]]. Let a smooth vacuum Bondi expansion be defined on an open retarded-length interval $I$. Then

$$\frac{dm_B}{du}=-\frac1{32\pi}\int_{S^2}N_{AB}N^{AB}\,d\Omega\le0.$$

If $dm_B/du=0$ throughout an open subinterval $J\subset I$ and $N_{AB}$ is continuous on $J\times S^2$, then $N_{AB}=0$ on $J\times S^2$.

references.title: Thomas Mädler and Jeffrey Winicour, Bondi-Sachs Formalism, arXiv:1609.01731 (2016), full 31-page PDF: §3, Eqs. (60)-(61), with the mass-aspect equation (58)

title: Null infinity, Bondi news and classical memory — Examples

items.title: A compact Bondi-news pulse with prescribed shear memory
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: Formal Bondi-boundary data with a constructed smooth Bondi-Sachs end and an imposed vacuum-form mass-aspect constraint; no Ricci-flatness, global vacuum solution, or observed waveform is asserted.
items.statement:
Let $\tau>0$ be a pulse length and let $a\ne0$ be a length. On the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$, let $q_{AB}$ be the unit round metric, $D_A$ its Levi-Civita derivative, and $d\Omega$ its area form. Put $Y(x)=\tfrac12(3x_3^2-1)$ and $T_{AB}=D_AD_BY-\tfrac12q_{AB}D^CD_CY$. Define the dimensionless bump $b(z)=e^{-1/(1-z^2)}$ for $|z|<1$ and $b(z)=0$ otherwise, let $Z=\int_{-1}^1b(z)\,dz$, and set $g_\tau(u)=b(u/\tau)/(\tau Z)$ and $\Phi_\tau(u)=\int_{-\infty}^u g_\tau(v)\,dv$. Then $g_\tau$ has units $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, support $[-\tau,\tau]$, and integral one. Set $C_{AB}=a\Phi_\tau T_{AB}$ and $N_{AB}=\partial_uC_{AB}=ag_\tau T_{AB}$. Impose the local coefficient constraint $\partial_um=\tfrac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\tfrac18N_{AB}N^{AB}$ on these formal boundary data, with $m(-\tau,x)=0$, and define $m_B(u)=\tfrac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}m(u,x)\,d\Omega$. It gives $\Delta C_{AB}=aT_{AB}$ and

$$m_B(\tau)-m_B(-\tau)=-\frac{a^2}{32\pi}\left(\int_{-\tau}^{\tau}g_\tau(u)^2\,du\right)\left(\int_{S^2}T_{AB}T^{AB}\,d\Omega\right)<0.$$

Let $r_0>0$ be a fixed inner radial cutoff with units of length. For the formal first-order detector response at a fixed sufficiently large area radius $r>r_0$, take a smooth screen-TT remainder $\rho_{AB}$ with $\sup_{[-\tau,\tau]}|\partial_u^j\rho_{AB}|\le K_jr^{-2}$ for $j=0,1,2$, where $K_j$ has dimensions $\mathrm{length}^{2-j}$, and put $H_{AB}=C_{AB}/r+\rho_{AB}$. In a fixed $q$-orthonormal screen basis, let $s_0^A$ be the initial separation and define $\delta s^A$ on $[-\tau,\tau]$ by $\partial_u^2\delta s^A=\tfrac12\partial_u^2H^A{}_B s_0^B$ with $\delta s(-\tau)=\partial_u\delta s(-\tau)=0$, raising indices with $q^{AB}$. Then $\delta s^A(\tau)=\tfrac{a}{2r}T^A{}_Bs_0^B+O(r^{-2}|s_0|)$; the formal clause alone makes no finite-amplitude error claim.

For any smooth normalized local metric family satisfying the quantitative clause of [[prop-gr-fx-memory-integral]] with this same $H$, use its initially covariantly comoving exact Jacobi field and parallel screen components $s_\lambda$. Then
$$s_\lambda(\tau)-s_0=\frac{\lambda a}{2r}T s_0+O(|\lambda|r^{-2}|s_0|)+O(\lambda^2|s_0|),\qquad s_\lambda'(\tau)=O(|\lambda|r^{-2}|s_0|)+O(\lambda^2|s_0|).$$
The amplitude-squared constants are for the fixed local family, tube and interval $[-\tau,\tau]$; $\lambda$ is its controlled dimensionless parameter. This does not assert Ricci-flatness of the constructed Bondi-Sachs end or identify that end with the local detector family.

items.title: Static supertranslation shear without Bondi news
items.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; readiness recorded separately.
items.physical_scope: A formal boundary-data example with an exact flat seed and finite shear action; it distinguishes shear from news and does not claim a full transformed vacuum metric or observation.
items.statement: Let $q_{AB}$ be the unit round metric on $S^2$, $D_A$ its Levi-Civita derivative, and $d\Omega$ its area form. On $I=\mathbb R$ and $r>r_0>0$, with $r_0$ a length, the exact flat Bondi metric is $g_0=-du^2-2du\,dr+r^2q_{AB}dx^A dx^B$; its shear, news and mass aspect are $C_{AB}=N_{AB}=m=0$. Let $m_B(u)=\tfrac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}m(u,x)\,d\Omega$. Let $Y(x)=\tfrac12(3x_3^2-1)$ on $S^2$, set $f=aY$ for a nonzero length $a$, and use the finite active boundary action $C^{(f)}_{AB}(u,x)=C_{AB}(u+f(x),x)-2D_AD_Bf+q_{AB}D^CD_Cf$, $N^{(f)}_{AB}(u,x)=N_{AB}(u+f(x),x)$. It gives $C^{(f)}_{AB}=-2aT_{AB}$, where $T_{AB}=D_AD_BY-\tfrac12q_{AB}D^2Y$, and $N^{(f)}_{AB}=0$. Treat these as formal boundary data with $m=0$ and impose the local coefficient constraint $\partial_um=\tfrac14D_AD_BN^{AB}-\tfrac18N_{AB}N^{AB}$. Then $m_B=0$, $dm_B/du=0$, and $\Delta C_{AB}=0$ on every retarded-time interval, where $\Delta C_{AB}=C_{AB}(u_2,x)-C_{AB}(u_1,x)$ for $u_1<u_2$. No full finite-transformed vacuum metric is asserted. A nonzero shear value alone therefore does not imply nonzero news or a nonzero shear difference.
